headings.text: Our mission is built on the belief that the cinematic lens can do more than just record history—it can act as the catalyst for its restoration. We organize our vision around three core pillars:

about.html.bodyText: About ZIFF our team COLLABORATIONS our partners GALLERY REGISTER REGISTER YOUR TEAM BECOME A VOLUNTEER donate! HELP FAQ REPORT RULES TOS PRIVACY BLOG CONTACT ABOUT ZIFF Learn More How It All Started Some lessons cannot be taught. They have to be lived, built and felt — in the nerves before a premiere, the excitement of seeing a project come together, and the applause at the end. Some of our most meaningful learning experiences have happened alongside young people, through projects that pushed us out of our comfort zones and brought us closer together. That is how the first Zoom In Short Film Festival came about — from courage, determination and a desire to do something that could make a difference. Together with the IBSB students volunteering with the “Adoptă o Casă” programme, we wanted to create more than a school event. We wanted a charity film festival open to young people from across Bucharest. We wanted to support the “Adoptă o Casă” programme in Roșia Montană, which has spent 15 years helping to preserve the area’s built heritage. And we wanted to hold the festival somewhere with a story of its own: Cinema Europa, Bucharest’s last remaining neighbourhood cinema, which is currently undergoing an exciting process of revitalisation. Getting there was intense, challenging and very real. There were Sunday mornings at 7 a.m. in the cinema, working on the festival’s visual identity, promotion, sponsorships, media partnerships, contracts, GDPR, automations and hundreds of messages. There were difficult decisions, unexpected problems and solutions we had to find along the way. Most of all, there was an extraordinary level of commitment. And the students did it not because they needed another line on their CVs. Most of them already had excellent opportunities ahead of them. They did it because they wanted to create something that mattered to someone beyond themselves. The idea itself was born from a setback. The previous year, we had tried to organise a film competition within our school, and it simply didn’t work. This time, we decided to open the doors wider. We thought perhaps 30 young people might enter. In the end, there were five. And you know what? Five was enough. Because every film took courage. Every young filmmaker had a voice. And we learned that success is not always measured in numbers. Sometimes it is measured by meaning. We are deeply grateful to everyone who supported us and encouraged us when we were beginning to doubt ourselves: Claudia Apostol, Andreea Duminicioiu, Cristiana Dumitru and the Cinema Europa team. We are grateful to our sponsors, Catena, UniCredit and HBO; our media partners, Euronews, ProTV and Frame Film; our jury, Corina Șuteu, Paula Antonia Cămîrzan and Mihai Mănescu; and Silvia Dragic and Tangaj Productions. Most of all, we are grateful to the young people who had the courage to submit their films and to everyone who came to watch them. Zoom In was more than a festival. It showed us what can happen when a team believes in an idea — and in a cause bigger than itself. And that was just the beginning. We are already preparing for the second edition, with even more enthusiasm for what comes next. The Zoom In Team: Theodor Aizic, Marc Paraschiv, Rareș Stanciu, Tommaso Bianchi, Andrei Stoenescu, Ecaterina Boțan, Rucsandra Florea, Sarmiza Bădeliță, Mara Mestecăneanu, Sofia McGregor, Aya Menner, Ilana Costache, Rita Bartoș, Petru Robatzchi and Johanna Croci Photography: Dragoș Ilie The "Zoom In" Philosophy Our mission is built on the belief that the cinematic lens can do more than just record history—it can act as the catalyst for its restoration. We organize our vision around three core pillars: Zoom In on the Screen ZIFF gives young filmmakers a space to share their stories and explore different ways of seeing the world. We welcome films that reflect the experiences, ideas and concerns of a new generation of storytellers, including documentary and realistic approaches. Through film, we want to turn places, people and stories that might otherwise be overlooked into something audiences can connect with — from the dust and stones of historic landscapes, to the stories of the communities that call them home. Zoom In on the Heritage We want to connect what happens on the cinema screen with the real work of preserving Roșia Montană’s historic buildings. The festival helps raise funds for the “Adoptă o Casă” programme, supporting restoration work carried out using traditional techniques and local craftsmanship, including lime-sand plastering, stone masonry and wooden shingle roofing. This helps preserve the buildings in a way that respects their history and original character. Zoom In on the Community ZIFF brings together young filmmakers, audiences and people working to preserve the heritage of Roșia Montană. We believe that film can do more than tell stories — it can start conversations, bring people together and inspire us to care about the places and communities around us. By connecting creative young people with the local community and the craftspeople who are helping to restore Roșia Montană, we hope to support a future in which its history, traditions and unique character can continue to be valued and shared. Our Impact & Legacy Festival Executive Summary Organized by Year 12 and 13 student volunteers from the International British School of Bucharest, the Zoom-In Film Festival 2026 combined youth artistic showcase with meaningful social impact. Hosted at Cinematograful Europa, the event featured a dual mission: supporting the Loc cu Loc cinema renovation campaign and fundraising for the ARA Association’s Adoptă o Casă la Roșia Montană program. Audience & Platform: Brought together ~100 in-person attendees and reached 2,130+ unique web visitors, giving high school filmmakers from Bucharest and Brașov a professional big-screen experience. Industry Expert Evaluation: Features five competing student short films judged by a distinguished panel including film critic Corina Șuteu, producer Paula Antonia Tudor-Cămîrzan, and screenwriter Mihai Mănescu, combined with real-time electronic audience voting. Strategic Sponsor Partnerships: Secured major corporate sponsorships and pro bono contributions from partners including Spring Farma, UniCredit Bank, HBO, Catena, and Frame Film. Sponsorships fully funded equipment vouchers, SKVOT directing courses, media internships, and all operational expenses. Direct Philanthropic Yield: Operating with complete cost efficiency, 100% of collected participation fees were directed straight to ARA’s historic preservation projects in Roșia Montană. 📄 View Full PDF Report Register Your Vision Join ZIFF 2027 and help define the pulse of a new generation. help.html.bodyText: About ZIFF our team COLLABORATIONS our partners GALLERY REGISTER REGISTER YOUR TEAM BECOME A VOLUNTEER donate! HELP FAQ REPORT RULES TOS PRIVACY BLOG CONTACT ZIFF 2027 Help Center & FAQ Welcome to the Zoom in Film Festival (ZIFF) Help Center. As an independent cultural entity, we are committed to providing a transparent and supportive experience for our community of filmmakers, partners, and audience members. Whether you are looking for technical submission details or information on our collaborative philanthropic model, you will find the answers here. FAQ 1. General Festival Information ZIFF (Zoom In Film Festival) is a short film festival dedicated to young filmmakers aged 14–21. It provides a platform for emerging creators to share their stories, showcase their work, develop their filmmaking skills, and connect with others who share their passion for cinema. The festival also supports the protection of built cultural heritage through its partnership with the Adopt a House in Roșia Montană programme. When and where will ZIFF 2027 take place? ZIFF 2027 is scheduled to take place in February 2027 in Bucharest. Further details about the date, venue, and programme will be announced closer to the event. Who is behind the festival? ZIFF is a youth-led initiative organised by the Cadru cu Cadru Association, bringing together young volunteers with a shared interest in film, creativity, and cultural heritage. The team is supported by an initiative group including Johanna Croci, Theodor Aizic, and Marc Paraschiv, who provide guidance throughout the planning and delivery of the festival. 2. Film Submissions & Competition Are submissions open? Yes! Submissions for ZIFF 2027 are now open. Young filmmakers aged 14–21 are invited to submit their short films and become part of the 2027 edition. What types of films can I submit? We welcome a wide range of short films, including fiction, documentary, animation, stop-motion, silent, and experimental films. All eligible films take part in the same competition and are evaluated according to the festival's official judging criteria. Can I submit a film in Romanian? Absolutely. Films can be in Romanian with English subtitles or English with Romanian subtitles. Subtitles should be clear, legible, and grammatically correct. Who can enter the competition? The competition is open to young filmmakers aged 14–21 who are enrolled in middle school, high school, or university. Teams can have up to five members, including actors, and each participant can be part of only one team. How long should my film be? Films must be between 7 and 10 minutes long, including credits. Are there any content restrictions? Yes. All films must be suitable for a teenage audience and comply with the festival's PG-13 content guidelines. Full details are available in the Official Regulations. Do I need parental consent to participate? If you are under 18, you will need written consent from a parent or legal representative to take part in the festival. 3. Donations & Supporting Our Cause What cause does ZIFF support? ZIFF is a charity event supporting the Adopt a House in Roșia Montană programme, initiated by the Architecture. Restoration. Archaeology (ARA) Association. The programme works to protect and rehabilitate the remarkable built cultural heritage of Roșia Montană. How does the festival contribute? Funds raised through festival registration fees are directed towards the Adopt a House in Roșia Montană programme, helping support its heritage conservation and restoration activities. How can I support the cause? You can support our mission by entering the festival, becoming a partner or sponsor, or making a donation. Details about available donation methods and ways to contribute are provided on our Donate Page. 4. Heritage Collaboration (ARA Association) Is ZIFF part of the Adoptă o Casă la Roșia Montană programme? No. ZIFF is organised independently by the Cadru cu Cadru Association and supports the Adoptă o Casă la Roșia Montană programme, initiated by the Arhitectură. Restaurare. Arheologie (ARA) Association. How does ZIFF support the programme? ZIFF supports the programme by raising funds through festival registration fees and by bringing greater visibility to the importance of protecting and preserving built cultural heritage. In this way, the festival connects the creativity and involvement of young people with meaningful heritage conservation efforts in Roșia Montană. Why does a film festival support cultural heritage? We believe that both film and built heritage preserve stories. By bringing the two together, ZIFF encourages young people not only to tell new stories through cinema, but also to recognise the value of protecting the places and histories that shape our shared cultural identity. 5. Ethics & Reporting How do you ensure a fair selection process? All eligible films go through a pre-selection conducted by three evaluators appointed by the festival organisers, using the same core criteria as the final judging process. Selected films are then evaluated by a jury with relevant professional experience in film and media. What standards of conduct are expected? ZIFF is committed to creating a respectful, inclusive, and safe environment. All participants are expected to follow the principles of fair play, respect, ethics, and safety throughout the festival. How can I report a concern? If you experience or witness inappropriate conduct or have concerns about fairness, please visit our Integrity & Fairness page or contact us at contact@zoomin-filmfest.com. We encourage participants to raise concerns so they can be addressed appropriately and responsibly. Still Need Help? Still Need Help? The Zoom In Film Festival (ZIFF) is a student-led film festival that brings together creativity, community and a passion for protecting cultural heritage. More than just an opportunity to showcase short films made by young people, ZIFF helps raise awareness and funds for the “Adoptă o Casă” programme in Roșia Montană, supporting efforts to preserve the area’s historic buildings and local heritage. By bringing young filmmakers and audiences together in Bucharest, the festival hopes to create a stronger connection between the city and the community of Roșia Montană — one that goes beyond the protests of 2013. Roșia Montană is a beautiful and diverse place, with a unique history that is worth protecting and sharing. There is still much work to be done to restore its historic buildings and help keep its heritage alive, and ZIFF is proud to support that effort through “Adoptă o Casă”. How It All Started Some lessons cannot be taught. They have to be lived, built and felt — in the nerves before a premiere, the excitement of seeing a project come together, and the applause at the end. Some of our most meaningful learning experiences have happened alongside young people, through projects that pushed us out of our comfort zones and brought us closer together. That is how the first Zoom In Short Film Festival came about — from courage, determination and a desire to do something that could make a difference. Learn More! Register YOUR MOVIE!

HELP FAQ REPORT RULES TOS PRIVACY BLOG CONTACT Press Room: Zoom in Film Festival 2027 Welcome to the official press hub for the Zoom in Film Festival (ZIFF) 2027. This edition represents an ambitious evolution of our mission to synthesize youth-led creative initiative with professional heritage conservation. ZIFF 2027 is more than a cinematic event; it is a vital dialogue between the urban transition of Bucharest and the rural continuity of Roșia Montană. Get started The ZIFF Mission The festival serves as the public-facing engine of a sophisticated philanthropic ecosystem dedicated to supporting the "Adopta O Casa" program. Our philosophy, "Zoom In," directs the cinematic lens toward endangered history to act as a catalyst for its physical restoration. By showcasing "engaged cinema"—powerful digital narratives that reflect values of creativity, innovation, and social responsibility—we aim to translate the "dust and stones" of the past into a restored future. 2027 Festival Highlights Authentic Venues: Moving beyond a single location, the 2027 edition inhabits authentic and inspiring cinema locations across Bucharest, creating an intimate environment for deep reflection on heritage and documentary realism [411, Conversation History]. Curatorial Focus: The program prioritizes "slow cinema" and documentary realism, featuring works that capture the pulse of a new generation of storytellers in a turbulent world. Direct Heritage Impact: Festival advocacy directly supports high-priority restoration projects managed by the ARA Association. Following the successful 2026 interventions at the Mining Museum’s Lapidarium and the Reformed Church, the 2027 campaign continues to fund traditional crafts and sustainable employment for local craftsmen. The Roșia Montană Connection Roșia Montană is a site of exceptional historical value, featuring over 2,000 years of mining history and the largest number of heritage monuments in any Romanian village. The ZIFF initiative serves as a primary pipeline for the Heritage Summer Campaigns, where cinematic engagement in the city transitions into hands-on restoration in the mountains. Participants and supporters contribute to the "scientific endeavor" of saving structures using traditional materials like lime-sand mortar and wooden shingles. Interviews: Interviews can be arranged with our Student Founders and our professional mentors, including Johanna Croci. Publications: Press members may request digital copies of our technical manuals, such as the Intervention Guide for Roșia Montană, which document the rigorous restoration methodologies supported by the festival. Registrations 1. Film Categories The Zoom In High School Short Film Festival welcomes young filmmakers working across a variety of styles, genres, and filmmaking techniques. Eligible submissions include: Short Fiction Films: live-action narrative films exploring original stories, themes, and creative perspectives. Short Documentary Films: non-fiction works exploring real people, experiences, communities, events, or subjects. Short Animated Films: films created using traditional animation, digital animation, stop-motion, or other animation techniques. Experimental and Silent Films: creative works that explore alternative approaches to cinematic storytelling and visual expression. All eligible films participate within the same competition and are evaluated according to the festival's official judging criteria. 2. Submission Guidelines & Eligibility Age Requirement: The competition is open to young filmmakers aged 14 to 21, enrolled in middle school, high school, or university. Team Structure: Each team may consist of a maximum of five members, including actors. Participants are free to distribute filmmaking roles, including directing, screenwriting, acting, cinematography, editing, and sound, within their team. A participant may not be part of more than one team during the same edition of the festival. Runtime: Submitted films must have a total duration of 7 to 10 minutes, including credits. Films that do not meet the required duration may be subject to point deductions or may be excluded from the competition. Language & Subtitles: Films may be submitted in Romanian, with English subtitles, or in English, with Romanian subtitles. All subtitles must be clear, legible, and grammatically correct. Originality & Copyright: Submitted films must be the team's original work. Any external music, images, footage, or other copyrighted materials may only be used if they are royalty-free or if the team has obtained the copyright holder's written permission. All external materials must be appropriately credited. Content Requirements: Films must be suitable for a teenage audience and comply with the festival's PG-13 content requirements outlined in the Official Regulations. For participants under the age of 18, written consent from a parent or legal representative is mandatory. 3. Technical Specifications All registrations must be completed through the official Zoom In Film Fest registration process. Films must meet the following minimum technical requirements: Format: MP4, MOV, or another compatible digital format approved by the organizers; Resolution: Minimum 1080p; Orientation: Landscape or portrait; Sound: Clear and intelligible, without significant distortion. Following registration, teams will receive instructions by email regarding the secure transfer of their film. Registration is considered complete only after: completing the official registration form; confirmation of payment of the participation fee; submission of the film according to the instructions provided by the organizers; and submission of signed parental consent forms for participants under 18. 4. Selection Process & Awards All eligible submissions will undergo a pre-selection process conducted by three evaluators appointed by the festival organizers. The pre-selection will use the same core criteria applied during the final judging process. Selected films will be screened during the official Zoom In Film Fest event and evaluated by a jury comprising professionals and individuals with relevant experience in film and media. Films will be assessed according to criteria including: Originality • Screenplay • Directing • Acting • Cinematography • Sound • Editing • Set Design • Creativity • Narrative Structure Prizes will be awarded for 1st Place, 2nd Place, and 3rd Place. Winners will receive diplomas, and additional prizes—such as filmmaking equipment, workshops, courses, or other professional development opportunities—may be awarded depending on the partnerships and resources available for the respective festival edition. The winners will be announced during the official Zoom In Film Fest Awards Gala. HELP FAQ REPORT RULES TOS PRIVACY BLOG CONTACT Integrity & Fairness ZIFF Ethics Reporting The Zoom In Film Festival (ZIFF) is committed to creating a fair, respectful, inclusive, and safe environment for everyone involved in the festival. As a youth-led initiative organised by the Cadru cu Cadru Association, we believe that creativity thrives in an environment built on respect, transparency, responsibility, and fair play. These principles guide not only our film competition, but also the way we work with participants, volunteers, partners, jury members, and audiences. This page provides a dedicated space for members of the ZIFF community to raise concerns about unfair treatment, inappropriate behaviour, ethical issues, or other conduct that may conflict with the values and regulations of the festival. Our Ethical Framework Fair Competition: All eligible films undergo a pre-selection conducted by three judges appointed by the festival organisers, using the same core criteria applied during the final judging process. Selected films are then evaluated by a jury with relevant experience in film and media. Respectful and Safe Environment: ZIFF does not tolerate abusive, discriminatory, intimidating, or dangerous behaviour. Everyone involved in the festival is expected to treat others with respect and to contribute to a safe and welcoming environment. Responsible Support for Cultural Heritage: ZIFF supports the Adoptă o Casă la Roșia Montană programme through funds raised from festival registration fees. We are committed to communicating clearly and responsibly about our charitable purpose and our collaboration with the Arhitectură. Restaurare. Arheologie. (ARA) Association. What You Can Report? We encourage the reporting of any issues that compromise the integrity or values of the festival, including: unfair treatment or concerns about transparency in the film selection or judging process; inappropriate, discriminatory, abusive, or unprofessional behaviour; conduct that may compromise the safety or wellbeing of participants, volunteers, or visitors; concerns about the responsible use of festival resources or the way our charitable and heritage partnerships are represented; other conduct that may conflict with the Official Regulations or values of ZIFF. Reporting and Resolution Process All concerns will be treated seriously, sensitively, and with appropriate discretion. Reports will be reviewed by the festival's designated team, and appropriate steps will be taken based on the nature and circumstances of the concern. You may choose to submit a report anonymously. However, providing as much relevant information as possible, including dates, circumstances, and any supporting information, will help us understand and appropriately address the issue. Our aim is to ensure that everyone involved with ZIFF can participate in an environment where creativity, fairness, respect, and responsibility are valued and protected. HELP FAQ REPORT RULES TOS PRIVACY BLOG CONTACT "Zoom In" High School Short Film Festival – Official Regulations A. General Information Festival Description: The "Zoom In" High School Short Film Festival is a competition dedicated to teenagers passionate about filmmaking and media production. The event is organized by the "Cadru cu Cadru" Association to provide a formal environment where young people can create, showcase, and share their visual productions. The official website of the festival is: www.zoomin-filmfest.com. Festival Purpose: The main purpose is to encourage creativity and artistic expression, develop technical and collaborative skills, and offer visibility in a professional setting. The festival is a charity event aimed at raising funds for the rehabilitation of heritage buildings included in the Adopt a House in Roşia Montană program, initiated by the Architecture. Restoration. Archaeology Association. Objectives: Supporting youth interested in the media field; Developing technical skills (filming, editing, sound, screenwriting, etc.); Stimulating initiative and teamwork; Creating an exhibition platform for youth cinematic creations; Financially supporting the Adopt a House in Roşia Montană program through donations obtained from the registration fees. B. Participants and Teams Eligibility: The competition is open to teenagers aged 14 to 21, enrolled in middle school, high school, or university. Team Structure: Each team can have a maximum of 5 members, including actors. The distribution of roles within the team (acting, directing, screenwriting, editing, sound, etc.) is up to the participants. A participant cannot be part of multiple teams during the same edition. Consent and Responsibility: Registration in the festival implies full acceptance of these regulations. For minor participants, the written consent of parents or legal representatives is mandatory. C. Film Eligibility Criteria and Technical Specifications Film Duration: Films must have a duration between 7 and 10 minutes, including credits. Failure to comply with the duration may lead to point deductions or rejection of the work. Technical Specifications: Recommended Format: MP4, MOV, or another compatible format (prior consultation with the organizer is recommended). Orientation: Landscape or portrait, at the team's choice. Image: Minimum resolution of 1080p. Sound: Clear, intelligible, without distortions. Film Language: Films can be in Romanian (with English subtitles) or in English (with Romanian subtitles). Subtitles must be clear, legible, and grammatically correct. Film Genre: All types of short films are accepted: live-action, animation, stop-motion, silent / experimental film, short documentary. Content Classification (General Audience / PG-13): All submitted films must be suitable for a teenage audience (PG-13 rating) and adhere to the following criteria: Violence Level: Graphic, extreme, or explicit violence (gore, mutilation, acts of gratuitous cruelty) is prohibited. Stylized or action violence is accepted only if moderate and relevant to the narrative context, without excessive bloody details. Sexual Content and Nudity: Explicit sexual content or directly simulated sexual acts are strictly prohibited. Only non-sexual nudity, brief or contextually suggested, without explicit undertones, is allowed. Language and Profanity: Excessive or aggressive vulgar language is prohibited. Moderate expressions are permitted only occasionally if essential for narrative realism. Prohibited Substances: Glorifying, promoting, or explicitly instructing the use of drugs or illegal substances is forbidden. Depicting the consumption of tobacco or alcohol is permitted only for narrative purposes, without being encouraged. Non-discrimination and Social Values: Any content including hate speech, discrimination (based on race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexual orientation, or disability), and incitement to violence or illegal acts is strictly forbidden. The selection committee reserves the right to automatically disqualify any work that exceeds the limits of the PG-13 rating or violates legislation regarding the protection of minors. Originality and Copyright: The film must be the team's original creation. The use of external music, images, or materials is allowed only if they are royalty-free or if the team has the author's written permission. The sources of the materials used must be mentioned in the final credits. Plagiarism or copyright infringement will result in immediate disqualification. D. Registration and Participation Fee Registration Fee: A fee is required and can be paid online on the "tickets.zoomin-filmfest.com" platform, managed in collaboration with the "Seaside Branding" agency (legally operated by Emil-Marc Paraschiv P.F.A.). Registration is valid exclusively after payment confirmation. Registration Process: Filling out the official form on the organizer's website. Sending the video content via secure transfer, according to the instructions received by email after registration. Sending the signed parental consent forms (for minors). Deadlines: Registration and payment: December 21, 2027, 23:59 EEST Film submission: February 1, 2026, 23:59 EEST Films submitted after the deadline may be refused or included exclusively in the non-competitive section. E. Selection, Judging, and Prizes Pre-selection: Will be conducted by 3 evaluators appointed by the organizers, based on the same criteria used in the final judging. The Jury: Selected films will be evaluated by a jury consisting of professionals and enthusiasts from the media field, during the official screening event. Judging Criteria: Originality; Artistic quality (screenplay, directing, acting); Technical quality (image, sound, editing); Set design; Creativity; Narrative structure. Prizes: Prizes will be awarded for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd Place. Diplomas and any additional prizes (workshops, equipment, etc.) will be awarded depending on available resources. Winners will be announced at the awards gala. F. Rights of Use and Promotion Copyright belongs entirely to the film creators. By registering for the competition, participants grant the organizers the non-exclusive right to broadcast the film: during the festival, on the organization's promotional channels, and in future presentation materials. The organizer is obliged to always mention the film title and the team's name. G. Conduct and Ethical Rules Participants commit to adopting respectful behavior. The organizers may disqualify any team that violates the principles of fair play, ethics, and safety. Abusive, discriminatory, or dangerous behaviors are strictly prohibited. H. Data Protection (GDPR) The processing of personal data (name, image, email, phone) is carried out in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR). For details regarding data subjects' rights, consult the Privacy Policy on the official website. I. Force Majeure and Fortuitous Events Neither party is liable for the failure to fulfill obligations if caused by force majeure (calamities, pandemics, restrictions) or fortuitous events (major technical failures not attributable to the organizer). The organizer reserves the right to postpone, modify the format (e.g., online), or cancel the event, notifying participants via email and the website. J. Final Provisions The organizers reserve the right to modify these regulations if the situation requires it, with any updates being announced publicly. Participation in the festival implies full acceptance of these regulations. Festivalul de Scurtmetraje pentru Liceeni „Zoom In” – Regulament Oficial A. Informații generale Descrierea festivalului: Festivalul de Scurtmetraje pentru Liceeni „Zoom In" este o competiție dedicată adolescenților pasionați de cinematografie și producție media. Evenimentul este organizat de „Asociația Cadru cu Cadru" pentru a oferi un mediu formal în care tinerii pot crea, prezenta și împărtăși propriile producţii vizuale. Pagina oficială a festivalului este: www.zoomin-filmfest.com. Scopul festivalului: Scopul principal este încurajarea creativității și a expresiei artistice, dezvoltarea abilităților tehnice și de colaborare, precum și oferirea de vizibilitate într-un cadru profesionist. Festivalul este un eveniment cu scop caritabil, menit să strângă fonduri pentru reabilitarea clădirilor de patrimoniu incluse în programul Adoptă o Casă la Roșia Montană, inițiat de Asociația Arhitectură. Restaurare. Arheologie. Obiective: Susținerea tinerilor interesaţi de domeniul media; Dezvoltarea competenţelor tehnice (filmare, montaj, sunet, scenariu etc.); Stimularea spiritului de iniţiativă și a lucrului în echipă; Crearea unei platforme de expunere pentru creațiile cinematografice ale tinerilor; Susținerea financiară a programului Adoptă o Casă la Roșia Montană prin donațiile obținute din taxa de înregistrare. B. Participanți și echipe Eligibilitate: Competiţia este deschisă adolescenților cu vârste cuprinse între 14 și 21 de ani, înscriși în învăţământul gimnazial, liceal sau universitar. Structura echipei: Fiecare echipă poate avea maximum 5 membri, incluzând actorii. Repartizarea rolurilor în echipă (actorie, regie, scenariu, montaj, sunet etc.) este la latitudinea participanților. Un participant nu poate face parte din mai multe echipe în cadrul aceleiași ediții. Consimțământ şi responsabilitate: Înscrierea în festival presupune acceptarea integrală a prezentului regulament. Pentru participanții minori, este obligatoriu acordul scris al părinţilor sau al reprezentanților legali. C. Criterii de eligibilitate pentru filme şi specificații tehnice Durata filmului: Filmele trebuie să aibă o durată cuprinsă între 7 și 10 minute, incluzând genericele. Nerespectarea duratei poate atrage depunctarea sau respingerea lucrării. Specificații tehnice: Format recomandat: MP4, MOV sau alt format compatibil (este recomandată consultarea prealabilă a organizatorului). Orientare: Landscape (orizontal) sau portrait (vertical), la alegerea echipei. Imagine: Rezoluție minimă de 1080p. Sunet: Clar, inteligibil, fără distorsiuni. Limba filmului: Filmele pot fi realizate în limba română (cu subtitrare în engleză) sau în limba engleză (cu subtitrare în română). Subtitrările trebuie să fie clare, lizibile și corecte din punct de vedere gramatical. Genul filmului: Sunt acceptate toate tipurile de scurtmetraj: live-action, animație, stop-motion, film mut / experimental, documentar scurt. Clasificarea Conţinutului (Audiență Generală / PG-13): Toate filmele înscrise trebuie să fie adecvate unui public adolescent (clasificare PG-13) și să respecte următoarele criterii: Nivel de violență: Sunt interzise scenele de violență grafică, extremă sau explicită (gore, mutilări, acte de cruzime gratuită). Violența stilizată sau de acțiune este acceptată doar dacă este moderată și relevantă contextului narativ, fără detalii sângeroase excesive. Conținut sexual și nuditate: Este strict interzis conținutul sexual explicit sau actele simulate direct. Este permisă doar nuditatea non-sexuală, scurtă sau sugerată contextual, fără încărcătură explicită. Limbaj şi vulgaritate: Este interzis limbajul vulgar excesiv sau agresiv. Expresiile moderate sunt permise doar ocazional, dacă sunt esențiale pentru realismul narativ. Substanțe interzise: Este interzisă glorificarea, promovarea sau prezentarea explicit-instructivă a consumului de droguri sau substanțe ilegale. Prezentarea consumului de tutun sau alcool este permisă doar în scop narativ, fără a fi încurajată. Non-discriminare şi valori sociale: Este strict interzis orice conținut ce include discurs de ură (hate speech), discriminare (pe criterii de rasă, etnie, religie, gen, orientare sexuală sau dizabilitate), incitarea la violență sau la acte ilegale. Comitetul de selecție își rezervă dreptul de a descalifica automat orice lucrare care depășește limitele clasificării PG-13 sau care încalcă legislația privind protecția minorilor. Originalitate și drepturi de autor: Filmul trebuie să fie o creație originală a echipei.
